title: 3Sum
kidExplanation: Find three numbers that add to zero. After sorting, fix one number and let two fingers hunt the rest.
plainProblem: 3Sum: Find three numbers that add to zero. Worked example — input: nums = [-1,0,1,2,-1,-4]; expected output: [[-1,-1,2],[-1,0,1]]. Why: Zero-sum triplets. Interview pattern to name out loud: Two pointers from both ends (or slow/fast).

thinkingSteps.title: Brute force idea
thinkingSteps.body: For “3Sum”, first say a correct slow approach: scan or retry every candidate until the example works by hand. Input nums = [-1,0,1,2,-1,-4] should still produce [[-1,-1,2],[-1,0,1]].

thinkingSteps.title: Why it is slow
thinkingSteps.body: Count the nested work. If each choice restarts a full scan, time blows up. Name the cost before optimizing — interviewers want that honesty. Target after the insight: O(n^2).

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: To find all unique triplets that sum to zero, we can use a three-pointer approach. First, we sort the input array 'nums' in non-decreasing order. Then, we iterate through the array with a fixed first element (i). For each fixed first element, we use two pointers (left and right) to find the other two elements that sum to the negation of the fixed first element. As the array is sorted, we can move these two pointers towards each other to efficiently find all possible triplets.

thinkingSteps.title: Better idea
thinkingSteps.body: Commit to Two pointers from both ends (or slow/fast). Sorted array, palindrome, or pair-sum hints. Walk example `nums = [-1,0,1,2,-1,-4]` → `[[-1,-1,2],[-1,0,1]]` while naming each variable, then code. Close with O(n^2) time and O(1) space.
